findings.fix: Remove this media query entirely or replace with a responsive layout that keeps content visible on all orientations.

findings.fix: Remove the style attribute to allow keyboard focus styles to display.
findings.violation: The inline style="outline:none" removes the keyboard focus indicator, making this link invisible to keyboard users navigating with Tab.

findings.evidence: <div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol" style="width:16px;height:16px">
findings.fix: Replace with a button element: <button class="icon-delete" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol" style="width:16px;height:16px">
findings.violation: Using a div with role="button" instead of a native button element means it lacks built-in keyboard support for Space and Enter keys without JavaScript.

findings.fix: Add aria-current="step" to the active step and use aria-disabled or similar attributes to indicate state.
findings.violation: The wizard steps have no ARIA attributes indicating which step is current, completed, or pending, reducing accessibility for assistive technology users.

findings.evidence: check the current station closures
findings.fix: Either change link text to match "/fares/history" (e.g., "check the fare history") or change href to match the text (e.g., "/closures").
findings.violation: The link text says "check the current station closures" but href points to "/fares/history", creating a mismatch between what users see and where the link goes.

findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label">Phone number (required)</label> followed by <input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">
findings.fix: Add required attribute: <input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel" required>
findings.violation: The label explicitly marks this field as required, but the input element lacks the required attribute.

findings.fix: Remove aria-invalid or set it to aria-invalid="false" initially, only setting to "true" after failed validation.
findings.violation: The aria-invalid="true" is hard-coded, making the field appear invalid to screen readers on page load before any user interaction or validation.
